title: The Day of the Smoky Hoodie
skyStory: Waning gibbous now, ninety-five percent, the moon has started its slow exhale. It's still in Sagittarius and still in a travelling mood, but it's taking the scenic route home. Tonight it hangs over every first campfire of the season like a nosy neighbour. Mars stokes the flames. Saturn sits upwind, wisely, with a blanket over its knees.

reading: First campfire of the year, if the weather cooperates, and the Fire Tiger is in its element. Literally. You'll build the fire perfectly, of course, and you'll want everyone to know it. Let them know it. Then hand someone else the poker.

Somewhere around the second log, conversation will turn deep in the way it only does around flames. Someone will tell you something real. Listen with your whole face. The [[Ten of Wands]] reversed says you don't have to carry their story for them; just hold it for a minute, then let the smoke take it up. Your hoodie will smell like woodsmoke for days. That's a feature.
joel.mission: Build or sit beside a fire tonight, even a candle, and tell one story you've never told before.
joel.omen: An ember drifting upward and winking out among the stars. Ideas don't need to last forever to light the way.

reading: The storyteller's night has arrived. When the fire settles and the faces turn orange, everyone will look at you. Your hands know what to do. Tell the one about the time you got lost and found something better.

The Wood Rat is clever enough to know when to stop: right at the best part, so they beg for more. Leave them hanging. Save the ending for tomorrow. The [[Page of Wands]] is sitting cross-legged in the front row, mouth open. Later, wrap yourself in the smokiest blanket and look up. The moon has shrunk by a whisker, but it's still bright enough to read by.
nancy.mission: Tell a story tonight and stop right before the ending. Promise to finish it tomorrow, then actually do.
nancy.omen: A log that suddenly flares up when you thought the fire was out. An old idea of yours has life in it yet.

together.text: Campfire summit. If either of you has a fire, a candle, or even a flashlight under a blanket, send a photo of the glow tonight. The other replies with a one-line ghost story, the less scary the better. Saturn's is about a chair that squeaks.
